## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Visākhātherīgāthā* (Thig 1.13, also cited as Thī 13) is a short canonical poem preserved in the *Therīgāthā* of the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya [Collett 2014]. The verse is ascribed to an elder nun (*bhikkhunī*) named Visākhā, who is distinct from both the prominent lay benefactress Visākhā (Migāra's mother) and the male lay disciple Visākha [Collett 2014].

**Sources**

- [Collett 2014] Alice Collett, ed., Women in Early Indian Buddhism: Comparative Textual Studies (2014) — Attribution of Thī 13 to the bhikkhunī Visākhā
